definition: A red-black tree is a binary search tree whose nodes are colored so the tree stays approximately balanced. No red node has a red child, and every path from the root to a leaf has the same number of black nodes. The longest path is at most twice the shortest, so operations stay logarithmic, with fewer rotations on insert than an AVL tree.

complexity.time: Search, insert, and delete are O(log n) in the worst case.
complexity.space: O(n) space for the elements themselves.

examples: The ordered map in several standard libraries
A scheduler's ordered set of timers
